base_instruction: You are a helpful food planning assistant. Help the user plan food for a tailgate party by tracking who is attending, their dietary needs, and preferences. When the user asks you to evaluate specific food items, check each item against every active attendee's current dietary constraints. Pay close attention to changes in the guest list and constraint updates throughout the conversation.

Jen is about 5 months pregnant now
Trying to keep it under $25 per person for food
My buddy Tommy is coming too, just confirmed. He's got a serious peanut allergy — carries an EpiPen and everything

Marcus just told me his flight got moved up, he's leaving Saturday morning now so he can't make the tailgate

Food list to check: beef sliders with brioche buns, Thai peanut chicken skewers, caprese salad, smoked salmon dip with crackers, black bean and corn salsa with tortilla chips, buffalo cauliflower bites

hidden_state.value: You are planning food for a tailgate party. You will introduce 5 friends with various dietary needs in a burst, then add a late-joining friend with a peanut allergy, upgrade one person's constraint from lactose intolerance to milk protein allergy, and have one person drop out. At the end you will present a list of 6 food items and ask if there are any issues. You never hint at what the problems might be.

You are a calm, easygoing person organizing a tailgate. You always refer to your friends by name in third person (e.g. 'Derek told me...', 'Priya texted me...'). You never express frustration or impatience when plans change. You treat each update as normal friend-group coordination.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation and ensures third-person relay

ground_truth.answer: Beef sliders with brioche buns: problematic for Derek (celiac — brioche buns contain gluten/wheat). Thai peanut chicken skewers: problematic for Tommy (severe peanut allergy). Caprese salad: problematic for Priya (contains fresh mozzarella — milk protein allergy, upgraded from lactose intolerance). Smoked salmon dip with crackers: problematic for Derek (crackers typically contain wheat/gluten) and potentially Priya (dip often contains cream cheese or sour cream — milk protein). Also note smoked salmon dip is fine for Jen as smoked salmon is cooked/cured, not raw. Black bean and corn salsa with tortilla chips: fine for everyone. Buffalo cauliflower bites: fine for everyone (no longer need to worry about root vegetables since Marcus left). Agent should NOT flag anything for Marcus's Jain diet since he is no longer attending.
required_elements: Beef sliders with brioche buns are problematic: Derek has celiac disease, brioche buns contain gluten
Thai peanut chicken skewers are problematic: Tommy has a severe peanut allergy
Caprese salad is problematic: Priya has a milk protein allergy (upgraded from lactose intolerance), fresh mozzarella contains milk protein
Smoked salmon dip with crackers is problematic: crackers contain gluten (Derek celiac), and the dip likely contains dairy (Priya milk protein allergy)
Black bean and corn salsa with tortilla chips is fine for all current attendees
Buffalo cauliflower bites are fine for all current attendees
forbidden_elements: Flagging any item for Marcus's Jain dietary restrictions (he is no longer attending)
Flagging caprese salad only for lactose intolerance (constraint was upgraded to milk protein allergy which is broader)
Saying Priya can have hard cheese or butter (milk protein allergy means ALL dairy is off limits, unlike lactose intolerance)
Flagging smoked salmon dip as unsafe for Jen due to pregnancy (smoked salmon is cured/cooked, not raw)
Flagging buffalo cauliflower bites as containing root vegetables for Marcus (he left)
ground_truth.explanation: This scenario tests entity lifecycle tracking with a constraint UPGRADE as the primary difficulty mechanism. Key tracking challenges: (1) Derek has celiac → must infer gluten-free requirement → brioche buns and crackers contain wheat. (2) Priya's constraint is UPGRADED mid-conversation from lactose intolerance to milk protein allergy — the agent must apply the BROADER constraint (all dairy banned, not just high-lactose items) to caprese salad and salmon dip. (3) Tommy joins late (Turn 3) with a severe peanut allergy — the peanut chicken skewers directly violate this. (4) Marcus EXITS (Turn 6) — his Jain restrictions (no meat, no root vegetables) should no longer be applied. The over-generalization trap: agents may flag smoked salmon as raw fish (unsafe for pregnant Jen), but smoked salmon is cured/cooked. The removed-entity trap: agents may still flag cauliflower bites or other items for Marcus's Jain diet. The upgrade trap: agents may still apply the narrower lactose intolerance rules (allowing hard cheese/butter) instead of the broader milk protein allergy rules.

mechanism: Constraint UPGRADE: an initial constraint is corrected to a broader one
